entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:1
segments: I am come into my garden, my sister, [my] bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; Drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:2
segments: I was asleep, but my heart waked: It is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, [saying], Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:3
segments: I have put off my garment; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:4
segments: My beloved put in his hand by the hole [of the door], And my heart was moved for him.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:5
segments: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands droppeth with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the bolt.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:6
segments: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself, [and] was gone. My soul had failed me when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:7
segments: The watchmen that go about the city found me, They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my mantle from me.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:8
segments: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, That ye tell him, that I am sick from love.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:9
segments: What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, O thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, That thou dost so adjure us?

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:10
segments: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:11
segments: His head is [as] the most fine gold; His locks are bushy, [and] black as a raven.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:12
segments: His eyes are like doves beside the water-brooks, Washed with milk, [and] fitly set.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:13
segments: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, [As] banks of sweet herbs: His lips are [as] lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:14
segments: His hands are [as] rings of gold set with beryl: His body is [as] ivory work overlaid [with] sapphires.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:15
segments: His legs are [as] pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: His aspect is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:16
segments: His mouth is most sweet; Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
